body:
**Issue Evaluation**

Category: `enhancement` (`area/harness`) | Status: **Evaluated — feasible, but blocked on an in-flight refactor** | Severity: **low-medium** (ergonomics / prompt-budget control)

**Claim-by-claim check** (verified against `main` @ `fefc196f4`, engine-assisted read of `agentscope-harness`)

| Claim | Result | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| `disableWorkspaceContext()` is the only switch today, and it is all-or-nothing | TRUE | `HarnessAgent.java:1259` (single boolean) → the whole `WorkspaceContextMiddleware` is skipped at `HarnessAgent.java:2529-2541` |
| No narrower switch disables only knowledge | TRUE | The Builder declares 16 `disable*` flags at `HarnessAgent.java:1232-1265` (compaction, toolResultEviction, filesystemTools, shellTool, webTools, memoryTools, memoryHooks, transcript, sessionPersistence, workspaceContext, atPathExpansion, subagents, dynamicSkills, defaultWorkspaceSkills, dynamicSubagents, toolsConfig); none gates knowledge. `disableMemoryTools()` / `disableMemoryHooks()` leave knowledge injection intact — `WorkspaceContextMiddlewareMemoryPromptTest:158-167` asserts `## Domain Knowledge` and `<domain_knowledge_context>` still appear when both are set |
| All four injection points are unconditional | TRUE | (a) `DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE_GUIDANCE` appended unconditionally in `buildGuidance()` — `WorkspaceContextMiddleware.java:260`; (b) `readKnowledgeMd(rc)` called unconditionally — `:216`; (c) `listKnowledgeFiles(rc)` catalog — `:574`; (d) both `WORKSPACE_FILES_NOTICE_*` templates name `knowledge/KNOWLEDGE.md` — `:113`, `:120`, selected at `:525-529` |
| Affected files are `WorkspaceContextMiddleware` + `HarnessAgent` | TRUE | exactly the four methods named in the report, plus the 6-arg middleware construction at `HarnessAgent.java:2531` |

There is also **no** alternative escape hatch today (no system property, env var, spec option or middleware flag). The only non-API workaround is to not ship a `knowledge/` directory, which is not viable for the reporter's setup. So the gap is real and the motivation (a custom retrieval tool competing with framework-injected "knowledge/ is the source of truth" guidance) is legitimate.

**Why no automated PR this tick — the proposed patch would collide with #3275.**

PR #3275 (OPEN, `+8148/-562`, by a project collaborator, opened ~1h50m before this issue; currently `REVIEW_REQUIRED`) rewrites the context pipeline these very methods live in:

- `buildWorkspaceSection()` stops emitting `<domain_knowledge_context>` via `buildXmlContext(...)` and instead emits `new ContextItem("knowledge", "workspace:knowledge", knowledgeBlock)` into a new `HARNESS_CONTEXT` model, with `ContextSelectionPolicy.defaults()` ranking `knowledge` second in the budget-omission order (after `memory`).
- `DOMAIN_KNOWLEDGE_GUIDANCE` is reworded, and both `WORKSPACE_FILES_NOTICE_WITH_MEMORY` / `..._WITHOUT_MEMORY` constants (the exact strings the prototype patch edits) are **deleted**.
- `HarnessAgent.java`, `HarnessAgentBuilderSupport.java` and all three `WorkspaceContextMiddleware*Test` classes are modified in the same PR.

So the diff attached to this issue cannot be applied as-is after #3275 lands, and if written now against `main` it conflicts on every touched hunk.

**Recommended direction** (maintainer call, since #3275 changes what "a switch" means):

1. If #3275 lands: express "no knowledge" as a per-source selection on the new context API (e.g. mark the `workspace:knowledge` source non-required / excluded, or a `ContextSelectionPolicy` that omits it unconditionally) rather than a new boolean threaded through the middleware constructor. This keeps one configuration model for the new pipeline instead of reintroducing the old flag pattern.
2. If a fix is wanted before #3275 settles: keep the flag on `HarnessAgent.Builder`, but add a `WorkspaceContextMiddleware` **overload** instead of changing the 6-arg constructor — `WorkspaceContextMiddlewareMemoryPromptTest:119`, `:139`, `:154` call that constructor directly, so a signature change breaks the build.
3. Either way, gating the *IO* (skip `readKnowledgeMd` / `listKnowledgeFiles` calls, not just discard their output) is worth keeping from the prototype — it is the part that avoids reading a 120K-document tree every turn.
4. `docs/v2/{en,zh}/docs/harness/*.md` has a switch table listing `disableWorkspaceContext()`; a new switch needs a row in both languages.

Testability: yes, no external services needed — a `WorkspaceContextMiddlewareKnowledgePromptTest` mirroring the existing memory-prompt test, asserting `## Domain Knowledge` guidance, the `KNOWLEDGE.md` body, the `Knowledge files:` catalog and the notice text are all absent when disabled while `AGENTS.md` / `MEMORY.md` / `<memory_context>` remain present.

@z43460018724 the requirement itself checks out — this is a genuine gap, not a misreading of the existing switches. The blocker is purely sequencing against #3275. If a harness owner confirms which of (1) or (2) they want, reply `/approve` or `/revise <direction>` and a patch will be generated against the agreed shape.

---
*Automated evaluation by github-manager-bot*

Update: PR #3275 (the in-flight context pipeline refactor that was blocking this issue) has been **closed without merging** on Sep 24 due to merge conflicts with main. The blocker no longer applies.

We have submitted **PR #3287** implementing the `disableKnowledgeContext()` approach (direction 2 — overload instead of changing the 6-arg constructor, per the evaluation's note about `WorkspaceContextMiddlewareMemoryPromptTest`).

PR #3287 is ready for review.

**Proposal window closed — no competing PR will be filed from this proposal window**

The 72 h feedback window opened by the evaluation above (2026-09-24T10:14:40Z) reached its bound with
no approve / revise / reject directive from a harness owner.

The thread answered the question in another way: @z43460018724 reported on 2026-09-24T21:59:10Z that
the sequencing blocker (PR #3275) had been closed without merging, and opened **PR #3287** —
`Fixes #3278`, direction 2 from the evaluation (a `WorkspaceContextMiddleware` overload rather than a
signature change on the 6-arg constructor). As of this read #3287 is OPEN, not a draft, review
decision APPROVED, 7/7 checks passing, `+398/-9` across 7 files, head `f87ba33cab`.

So the implementation path for this request is owned by a community PR that already exists and is
awaiting maintainer merge. Filing a second PR against the same issue is exactly the collision this
window policy exists to prevent, so the proposal is stood down and no automated PR will be generated
from it.

Nothing here disputes the evaluation: the gap is real and the recommended shape is the one #3287
implements. Merge, close, or request changes on #3287 — that is the productive thread now. If #3287 is
closed unmerged and this remains wanted, reopen the question on #3278 and it will be re-evaluated
against whatever `main` looks like at that point.

*Automated feedback-window maintenance by github-manager-bot*
